title: Compact adapter patterns for polyglot fetch and streaming
creator: Marta Alvarez
description: Define a lightweight adapter pattern and acceptance criteria for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that lets customers use a single, compact client surface for both paginated RPC fetches and streaming responses. This ticket captures product requirements, API ergonomics, backward compatibility constraints, and rollout guidance for gradual adoption.
problem_statement: Many customers have mixed workloads: synchronous paginated RPCs for list and analytics endpoints, and long-lived streaming responses for generation. Existing SDKs have diverged shapes for pagination vs streaming (cursor-based iterators vs streaming callbacks), causing duplicate app-level logic, inconsistent retry semantics, and painful migrations across runtime changes or model fallbacks. We need a unified, minimal adapter pattern so client apps can switch between fetch and stream without complex branching logic.
goals: Design a compact adapter API that wraps: paginated fetch (cursor token), windowed streaming (short-lived chunked streams), and resumable streams where supported
Provide canonical examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs demonstrating migration paths and minimal code changes
Specify clear retry and idempotency rules that are consistent across fetch and stream modes
Ensure backward compatibility: no breaking surface changes for existing public methods; new adapters are additive
Define automated acceptance tests and performance SLOs for adapter-backed flows
non_goals: Rewriting all SDK paging primitives — adapters are additive and opt-in
Changing server-side cursor semantics in this ticket (server changes will be separate)
Implementing full resumable persisted checkpoints for very long streams — only short window resume (<= 60s) is in scope
requirements_functional: Provide an Adapter abstraction that exposes a single iterate() method on all three SDKs which yields item records for paginated RPCs and streaming partials for stream endpoints
Adapter must accept a configuration object: {mode: 'fetch' | 'stream', page_size, resume_window_seconds, max_prefetch_pages, idempotency_key (optional)}
Fetch mode behavior: use server-provided cursor token; adapter should auto-prefetch up to max_prefetch_pages when caller iterates
Stream mode behavior: open streaming connection; adapter must buffer small windows and expose same iterate() protocol

Resume behavior: when resume_window_seconds > 0, adapter should attempt tail-resume on transient disconnects within the window by reissuing requests with server hints (cursor or message_id) if server supports resume

Fallback behavior: when stream endpoint is unavailable or throttled, adapter may fall back to paginated fetch mode transparently if the server advertises a compatible RPC; this fallback must be controllable by client config
Inspector hooks: expose telemetry callbacks for token_cost, latency_ms, and retry_count to the host application
Error surface: distinguish recoverable transient errors (adapter retries) vs terminal errors (propagated to caller). Provide structured error codes documented in SDKs
requirements_nonfunctional: Adapter iterate() must maintain low allocation overhead and keep per-item latency within 25% of native fetch/stream in benchmarked workloads
Default retry/backoff must match platform SLO guidance (exponential backoff with jitter, initial_delay=200ms, max_attempts=5)
Memory bounds: adapter should cap internal buffering to configured page_size * max_prefetch_pages where applicable
Telemetry: SDKs must emit standardized labels for adapter flows: adapter_name, mode, fallback_used, resume_attempted
Compatibility: adding Adapter must not change existing public function signatures — provide helper factories rather than replacing constructors
api_surface_examples:
Python example:
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
adapter = client.adapters.compact(mode='stream', page_size=50, resume_window_seconds=30)
for item in adapter.iterate(endpoint='responses.stream_generation', prompt='...'):
    process(item)
pagination_semantics: Preferred pagination is server-driven opaque cursor tokens. Adapter must treat cursors as opaque strings and only forward them back to server calls. Offset-based pagination may be supported as a shim when cursorless endpoints are detected, but it must be explicitly enabled and flagged in telemetry.
retry_semantics: All SDKs: default to idempotency-aware retries. Non-idempotent write endpoints are not to use Adapter iterate() by default
Retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, initial=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max=5 attempts
On streaming partials: retry may re-open stream and re-request the last acknowledged message; adapters must persist a lightweight last_seen marker when resume_window_seconds>0
Network blips: immediate soft retry (fast path) for common ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT errors before applying full backoff
Telemetry must record retry_count and last_retry_cause
streaming_contract: Adapters must surface streaming chunks as same unit type as paginated items (i.e., normalized record shape)
Short-window resumability: if server supports a resume token or message_id, adapter should use it to request missing tail messages
Backpressure: clients using iterate() must be able to signal slow consumption; SDK must throttle prefetch accordingly
Heartbeat keepalives: adapter should support an optional keepalive to avoid idle disconnects for long-running streams
compatibility_strategy: Additive SDK change: expose client.adapters.compact(...) factory; existing methods remain unchanged
Migration doc: provide a step-by-step guide to convert list/stream client code to Adapter in single-digit code edits
Feature flags: ship adapter behind a 'compact_adapters' feature toggle for 6 weeks before enabling by default
Cross-language parity: API names and core option keys must be consistent across Python/TS/Go; language idioms accepted for naming conventions
Deprecation policy: if server-side cursor semantics change later, follow 90-day deprecation and provide automated client warnings
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize API spec, design reviews with SDK leads (Python/TS/Go)
Week 3-6: implement adapters in parallel feature branches, implement unit and integration tests against testserver harness
Week 7: e2e dogfood in Redwood internal apps and one pilot customer integration
Week 8-9: enable feature flag for 50% of accounts (no default), collect telemetry and bug reports
Week 10: GA release behind beta docs; default enable after monitoring for 2 weeks
acceptance_criteria: API parity: examples above compile/run in their respective SDKs and adapters are reachable via factory methods
Behavioral tests: adapter.iterate() yields same sequence of logical records when called against (a) paginated fetch and (b) streaming endpoint that emits equivalent records
Resume test: simulated transient disconnect within resume_window_seconds must result in successful resume without data duplication for canonical scenario
Fallback test: when stream endpoint returns 503 and server advertises fetch fallback, adapter must switch to fetch mode when fallback_enabled=true
Performance: adapter overhead measured in benchmark harness must be <25% extra latency per-item and memory bounded as specified
Telemetry: adapter flows emit required labels and retry_count metrics to the ingestion pipeline
dependencies: runtime:server-side hinting for resume_token (server change in separate ticket)
sdk:SDK transport layer must support last-seen markers and reconnection helper APIs
console:observability: add adapter labels to ingestion and dashboards
stakeholders: SDK leads: Priya Nair (Python), Ben Fischer (TypeScript), Daniel Wu (Go)
open_questions: What is the canonical unit for iteration when stream chunks are partial text delta vs final records? Do we normalize to final records or deliver deltas to callers?
Should adapters persist last-seen markers to disk for multi-process resume, or limit to in-memory resume within the process?
What is the recommended default for max_prefetch_pages across languages given different GC/alloc characteristics?
When falling back from stream->fetch, how do we ensure no record loss or duplication if server-side delivery guarantees differ?
